category_title: Sociable and determined children with physical and cognitive impairments
minimal_context: Mandy is sitting at the snack table with other children, trying to get a drink of milk.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for snack. I am passing out the drinks and food now.

STUDENT: (Waits patiently while the adult helps another child, then reaches out to try to take a cup the adult is holding.)

TUTOR: Waiting Mandy, waiting.

STUDENT: (Takes the cup and pulls it towards her to drink.)

TUTOR: Pouring, good girl. (Takes the cup from her with no explanation and turns to another child)

STUDENT: (Reaches out to take the bottle of a passing child, then bangs her open hand on the table using a signal for 'more'.)

options.A: Creating opportunities for staff in early years settings to observe children with learning disabilities in their optimal communication environments.
options.B: Adding a visual schedule to make the snack routine explicit, using a series of pictures showing Mandy completing each step of pouring milk.
options.C: Implementing daily activities focused on recognizing, understanding, and accepting a wide range of feelings, teaching the distinction between feeling and behaving.
options.D: Compromising, negotiating situations, and sharing decisions and power with the student during snack time instead of imposing adult control.
